text:
alex.k: FYI we need a planned window to rebalance the eu-gpu-pool and swap priority racks. target: Sat 02:00 UTC. planning a staggered node reboot + affinity reshuffle. expect brief evacuations (~2-5m per node). :calendar:

tara.ops: ETA on total capacity hit? any Dedicated customers that will see degraded throughput?

alex.k: We should keep Dedicated at >=85% of baseline. Plan is to spin up 4 warm spares in az-eu1 before drains, then move low-priority workloads to quantized variants. That should hedge latency spikes.

jordan-sre: Can you paste the drain command we plan to run so oncall can monitor? also add a network QoS fallback if egress queues get saturated.

alex.k: Drain snippet below — use `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and stagger 30s between nodes:

```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-XX
kubectl drain gpu-node-XX --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```

nicole-eng: We also need to update the smart-router policy for this window to prefer low-latency regions for customer tiers. Suggest the following temporary routing patch: set `eu-priority` pool weight +30, and add fallback to `eu-spot-quant` for non-critical inference.

liam-sre: Cost question — spinning warm spares increases hourly burn. How long will spares be up? recommend creating them 1hr before, tear down within 30m after window. that keeps delta small.

alex.k: Agreed. Warm spares up at 01:00 UTC, drains start 02:00 UTC, window ends ~04:00 UTC. tear down spares at 04:30 UTC. Total extra run-hours = ~3.5 * 4 instances. approving cost with finance?

tara.ops: I'll loop in finance and support. @support please prep canned replies for customers in case SLAs are impacted. also update status.redwood.ai with maintenance banner at 01:30 UTC. :loudspeaker:

infra-bot: Maintenance scheduled by alex.k — ID MNT-2034567890. Window: 2025-11-08T01:00:00Z to 2025-11-08T04:30:00Z. Automated pre-checks will run at -45m and -10m.

jordan-sre: Pre-checks: node health, nvlink status, kernel page cache pressure, and egress QPS baseline. If any pre-check fails, abort and escalate. I'll add a gating check to the runbook.

nicole-eng: One more: there's a pending NIC microcode push on az-eu1 that conflicts with maintenance. we should either postpone that microcode or sequence it after our reboots. I'd prefer we postpone the NIC push by 48h to avoid double reboots.

alex.k: Postpone NIC push — agreed. I'll file a change to the firmware team.

liam-sre: For rollback: if we see >20% median p95 latency increase for Dedicated customers for 15m, we immediately stop further drains and start reverts — move traffic to us-west fallback pool and bring spares to handle load.

tara.ops: Support playbook: short notice banner, targeted emails to Dedicated contacts, channel #support-escalations open for customer-facing updates. I'll own comms.

infra-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/mnt-2034567890 — prechecks, drain order, rollback steps, and cost estimate attached.

alex.k: Great. Next steps: tara to publish banner, nicole to postpone NIC push, jordan to add gating checks, liam to prepare fallback pool, I'll create the tracker and notify sales for dedicated customers. Thanks. :thumbsup:
